The book unifies these two strands into a single category rather than treating them as separate contexts. 1 Peter 1:7 (refined like gold) and Revelation 13:16/14:1 (mark of the beast) extend the image motif beyond the tribute coin, while Exodus 30:12–16 and Leviticus 27:2 supply the 'assigned value' dimension.   "extension_reasoning": "The book adds the 'beast' image (Rev 13:16) and the refinement motif (1 Pet 1:7) not present in the 1st-century tribute or lost-coin passages, and it reclassifies the widow's mites (Mark 12:41–44) as evidence that human valuation differs from God's. It also includes the census/ransom money (Ex 30) and temple-tax coin (Matt 17:27) as illustrations of value and provision. These are boundary expansions rather than contradictions; the consensus already lists image-bearing and lost-sinner readings as common, so the book is refining their scope and interrelation rather than replacing them.
